key_insight: The paper proposes a model-agnostic audit that separates real privacy leaks from incidental synthetic matches by statistically testing synthetic outputs against held-out control data.
engineering_relevance: It gives practitioners a low-cost way to measure privacy leakage in synthetic data systems without needing model access, canaries, or shadow models.
method: Partition data into train and holdout sets
Compare synthetic outputs to a held-out control set using hypothesis tests
Classify matches as true disclosures or phantom disclosures and benchmark against zero-learning or DP baselines
evidence_signal: The framework is evaluated as an empirical lower-bound audit that detects disclosures consistent with membership inference behavior while using far fewer resources than prior auditing methods.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality of the holdout control set and the validity of the chosen privacy baseline, so weak controls can make leakage estimates misleading.
paper_title: Phantoms and Disclosures: a Causal Framework for Auditing Synthetic Data
